01 · The Problem We Investigate
Did growing through mergers make JPMorgan Chase stronger, or too big to fail?
Our hypothesis: both. Size built strength and risk at the same time.
1How did it grow?Origins · Growth · Mergers
2What did size give it?Business lines · Global reach · Technology
3What risks came with size?The 2008 crisis · The evidence board
systemic risk = one failure can hurt the whole financial system
too big to fail = so large that a government may have to rescue it
bailout = public money used to save a company
02 · The Origins

Origins

1799
A water company that became a bank
  • A yellow fever outbreak pushed New York to find clean water
  • Alexander Hamilton and Aaron Burr led the effort; the Manhattan Company was founded
  • Burr added a provision to the charter: extra funds could open a bank
  • Within six months, the Bank of the Manhattan Company opened. Water service ended in 1842
Clue for our problemThe first financial institution in the family tree began by accident, then outlived its water business.
03 · The Growth

Growth

1871
Banking for a growing nation
  • J. Pierpont Morgan joins Anthony Drexel: Drexel, Morgan and Company
  • They finance America's railways and steel industry
  • Power grows through partnerships and the acquisition of smaller companies
  • 1895: renamed J.P. Morgan and Company. 1901: helps create U.S. Steel. 1907: steps in during a bank panic
Clue for our problemThe bigger the banker became, the more the whole system leaned on him in a crisis.
03 · The Growth

Forced Apart

1933
A new law splits banking in two
  • The Glass–Steagall Act separates investment banking from commercial banking
  • J.P. Morgan and Co. chooses to stay a commercial bank
  • 1935: Henry S. Morgan and Harold Stanley found Morgan Stanley as the investment bank
  • 1940: J.P. Morgan and Co. becomes a public company; Jack Morgan is first chairman
Clue for our problemRules decide how big a bank may become: tightened in 1933, relaxed again in 1999.
J.P. Morgan and Co.before 1933 · all kinds of banking
J.P. Morgan and Co.commercial banking
stays with the original bank
Morgan Stanleyinvestment banking
founded 16 September 1935
1933law passed
1935the split is complete

04 · The Mergers, continued

Crisis Year: 2008

March – May 2008Bear StearnsA rescue deal announced on 16 March at $2 a share, later raised to about $10. Completed on 30 May.
25 September 2008Washington MutualJPMorgan buys most of WaMu's banking operations from the FDIC for about $1.8 billion.
28 October 2008$25 billion in TARP fundsPublic money flows to JPMorgan Chase as part of a government programme to steady banks. It was repaid in 2009.
2004 – 2006Jamie DimonJoins after the Bank One merger in 2004, becomes CEO in December 2005 and chairman in December 2006.
Clue for our problemSize let the bank buy two failing rivals, and the same year it accepted public money. Strength and risk at once.

07 · SGH and Students

Why SGH?

Where Poland's future bankers study
  • Founded in 1906: the oldest and most prestigious business school in Poland
  • The Student Union speaks for all students in the School's Senate
  • About 80 student organisations are listed, including Investors' Club and Klub FINTECH
  • Clubs run talks, workshops and company events, a bridge between students and employers
Why it mattersA bank that wants finance talent goes where finance students are, and student clubs open the door.
1906year founded
9.4Kstudents, Dec 2023
~80student organisations
07 · SGH and Students

How the Bank Works with Students

1Campus eventsThe Early Careers team in Warsaw runs a "campus season" of events at universities, often with student clubs.
2Insight events and internshipsSpring insight events and summer internship programmes give a first look inside the bank.
3Working StudentSeptember to May, about 8 months, 20 hours a week, on site in Warsaw. Areas include KYC, HR and supplier services.
4Analyst programmesThe team places more than 1,000 early-career hires into entry-level analyst roles across the firm.
Who can applyFluent EnglishMS OfficeInterest in finance, economics or lawGraduating within about a year
Source: public JPMorganChase Warsaw job postings, 2025 – 2026.
08 · Verdict

Strength or Risk?

Size made it stronger

  • In 2008 it bought Bear Stearns and WaMu's banking operations
  • Four lines of business and clients in 100+ countries
  • $4.4T in assets and about 318K employees
  • About $19.8B planned for technology in 2026

Size made it riskier

  • Considered systemically important by the Financial Stability Board
  • $25B in public TARP funds in 2008, repaid in 2009
  • The 2012 "London Whale" trading loss: about $6B
  • Every merger (Chemical, Bank One, Bear Stearns, WaMu) adds complexity
Our reading: both are true. The same size that rescued rivals also made the bank too important to fail quietly.
08 · Conclusion

Conclusion

Mergers made JPMorgan Chase bigger, stronger and systemically important, all at the same time.
